query: What drives praise and complaints in Amazon reviews?

per_column.name: praise_word_count
per_column.rationale: A bare count of praise words is a mechanical proxy for the presence of praise itself, not a distinct constitutive aspect of what DRIVES praise. It restates the sentiment magnitude rather than naming a driver (e.g., product quality, price, delivery).

per_column.name: complaint_word_count
per_column.rationale: Symmetric to praise_word_count: a count of complaint words measures the complaint signal, not an aspect/facet of the underlying drivers. It also overlaps heavily with praise_word_count as a generic polarity-count pair.

per_column.name: review_detail_level
per_column.rationale: How detailed a review is may correlate with review informativeness but is not a part-of the drivers of praise/complaint; it is a property of the review text, an external predictor at best.

per_column.name: emotional_intensity
per_column.rationale: Generic sentiment/emotion intensity is a bare affect measure. It captures how strongly the reviewer feels, not WHAT drives that feeling, so it restates polarity strength rather than decomposing the drivers.

per_column.name: aspects_discussed
per_column.rationale: A single count of aspects discussed points toward the right idea (drivers are product/service aspects) but does not itself enumerate any facet; it is a meta-count, not a named constitutive aspect such as quality, price, shipping, or usability.

judge.rationale: The concept 'praise_and_complaint_drivers' should decompose into constitutive aspects that people praise or complain about -- e.g., product quality, price/value, shipping/delivery, customer service, usability, durability. None of the added columns name such facets. Instead they are mechanical magnitude measures (praise/complaint word counts, emotional intensity), text-property proxies (detail level), or a bare aspect count. praise_word_count and complaint_word_count are near-mirror generic polarity counts that overlap in what they capture, and emotional_intensity again reflects polarity magnitude, lowering mutual exclusivity. Since no genuine driver facet is present, exhaustiveness against the concept is near zero. The set fails the meronymy test.
